That last one touches nothing under upgrades/engine, so no PROVENANCE row moved. The clone at clonePath is gitignored (vendor/) and has its own .git pushing to the personal fork. pushed:true records that the branch is on that remote: pushed 2026-09-10 at the owner's explicit ask, a fast-forward d49096e9 -> 0b50f402, verified with `git -C vendor/tbc-new-fork ls-remote origin refs/heads/feat/upgrades-tab` returning this file's commit. That closes ticket 355 -- before the push the pin existed on one disk while data/sim-implemented-effects.json embedded it, so those committed artifacts were unre-derivable anywhere else. Flipping this flag stays a deliberate act: a later fork commit moves commit ahead of the remote again, so re-verify with ls-remote rather than trusting the flag. Nothing but line endings changed -- all 29 were measured two ways before the write (CR-stripped byte compare and `json.loads` equality, agreeing on every file), and afterwards `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol` over upgrades/data/ is empty while the plain diff reports 463442 insertions against 463442 deletions. The recurrence itself is now ticket 399: sync_fork_universes.py compares working-tree bytes and neither side's line endings are pinned -- the core normalises only on commit via .gitattributes and this fork has no .gitattributes at all, so the core tree currently sits split 47 CRLF / 41 LF purely by regeneration batch (every CRLF file stamped 2026-09-14 09:59, every LF file 15:22). Clearing the symptom does not stop the next regen re-redding the gate. `pushed` stays **false**: the remote is now two commits behind, `git -C vendor/tbc-new-fork ls-remote origin refs/heads/feat/upgrades-tab` returning 2781486d6b324c3092c0c5dcd51a26bbb7103d78 at the time of writing, so both eb040855c and this commit exist on one disk only -- the ticket-355 exposure ADR-0030 Consequence 4 accepts. As of e94d927af (2026-09-15, ticket 399) the recurrence the previous entry described is fixed from both sides rather than cleared again. Fork side: this commit adds a .gitattributes at upgrades/data/ pinning `* text eol=lf`, staged with `git add --renormalize` so the already-committed blobs move -- 15 copies were committed CRLF (ret-p2 5603 CR, warrior-p2 15350 CR, and 13 others), and a worktree refresh alone would have left them that way. `git check-attr text eol` on those copies went from both unspecified to `text: set` / `eol: lf`. It is scoped to that directory, not the fork root, because every future merge from wowsims/tbc-new carries a fork-local dotfile and only these copies need the guarantee. Core side (commit 871bb748 in this repo): 13 write_text( call sites across 11 scripts omitted `newline=`, so Windows text mode wrote CRLF into the working tree that sync_fork_universes.py byte-compares; all 13 now pass `newline="\n"`, and regenerating all 44 universes and 44 reports took data/universes/ from 47 CRLF / 41 LF to 0 CRLF / 88 LF. The 47/41 split the previous entry recorded is therefore historical, not current. No committed data artifact changed in this repo: the .gitattributes catch-all normalises on staging, so those blobs were LF throughout and the regenerated tree is byte-identical to HEAD -- only the worktree had alternated, which is exactly what the gate reads.
